failure: The CSS canon guard rejected a new experience-switch hover literal
root_cause: The implementation duplicated the canonical hairline color as a raw rgba literal
fix: Replaced the literal with var(--hairline) and reran both CSS and texture canon guards successfully
lesson: New visual seams must consume existing canon tokens before the first final guard run

failure: The first full frontend rerun failed one EmergencyControl assertion even though its fetched DOM state said the latch was engaged
root_cause: The test observed the rendered resource data before the component's passive effect had published that same observation to the external emergency-stop presentation store
fix: Waited on getEmergencyStopPresentation() in the regression so the assertion targets the authoritative external-store transition; no production code changed
lesson: When a UI render and an external presentation store are updated in separate React effects, tests must await the store boundary rather than infer synchronization from visible DOM text

failure: The first constrained full-suite command exited before running tests because Vitest does not support the supplied --minWorkers flag
root_cause: A worker flag from a different test-runner invocation was used without checking the installed Vitest CLI options
fix: Reran with the supported --maxWorkers=1 option; the full suite passed 154 files / 841 tests
lesson: Use the repository's installed test-runner invocation for long evidence runs; do not add unsupported concurrency flags

failure: The first port-unit command reported npm run test:port missing
root_cause: The command was launched from the repository root even though the frontend package owns that script
fix: Reran from frontend; all 5 port-unit tests passed
lesson: Run package-owned frontend gates from the package directory and record root-versus-package scope explicitly

failure: The first focused Vitest command exited without running tests
root_cause: A repository-relative filter was used while the command ran from the frontend package directory
fix: Reran with src-relative paths and required an actual test-file count before interpreting the gate
lesson: Align test filters with the declared working directory and reject zero-file results as evidence

failure: The first reduced-motion reactive-effects test never terminated, and the first lint run rejected a ref synchronization added during render
root_cause: The test mock returned a new BeingPresentation object on every render, retriggering a dependent worker effect; the production patch assigned a ref during render under the repository's React lint rules
fix: Stabilized the hoisted mock object and moved reducedMotionRef synchronization into useEffect; focused tests, full suite, typecheck, build, lint, and guards then passed
lesson: R3F seam tests must preserve semantic object identity, and shared preference refs must be synchronized through effect boundaries when the lint contract forbids render-time ref writes

failure: The first post-coherence full serial suite failed EmergencyControl's clear-latch assertion with the DOM updated but the external stop-presentation store still unknown
root_cause: The test waited for fetched resource DOM text but asserted a store value published by a separate passive effect; the race appeared in multi-file serial execution and was hidden by the isolated file run
fix: Added a condition-based wait for the external store, reproduced the two-file failure before the change, and reran the complete suite successfully
lesson: When a UI assertion crosses a React DOM boundary into an external store, wait for the store's authoritative condition rather than treating DOM readiness as synchronization

failure: The first focused coach-copy run failed an existing default-Guided assertion that expected the former internal approval wording
root_cause: The test fixture rendered the default Guided mode while asserting the Expert-era phrase; the product copy change correctly removed that phrase from Guided
fix: Updated the test to assert the human-language Guided sentence and kept the internal wording covered by an explicit Expert render
lesson: When a product vocabulary boundary changes, make test mode explicit instead of allowing default-mode assumptions to preserve stale copy

failure: npm run port:check still failed after the copy-only change
root_cause: The dedicated worktree intentionally lacks the ignored GAG demo lab tree; the first required lab source components/QualityTierProvider.tsx is absent
fix: Did not copy or edit generated Superbrain files; recorded the blocker and retained the prior read-only main-checkout diagnosis
lesson: A clean product worktree cannot prove a lab-owned port check when the lab tree is absent; stop at the ownership boundary instead of manufacturing sources

failure: The first port:check invocation used the repository root and npm reported that the frontend script was missing
root_cause: The command was run from the worktree root instead of the frontend package directory
fix: Reran the command from frontend; it reached the expected lab-source ownership blocker at components/QualityTierProvider.tsx
lesson: Run package scripts from the package directory and distinguish command-location errors from the genuine generated-source port boundary

failure: The first route-history regression fixture failed typecheck because summary-only recent-event types do not declare payload
root_cause: The adapter safely accepts richer admitted event payloads at runtime, but the store's public test type intentionally models the summary-only boundary
fix: Marked only the richer route fixture as a test-only admitted shape with an explicit never cast; runtime code and type boundary remain unchanged
lesson: When testing truth that is intentionally richer than a summary type, isolate the cast to the fixture instead of widening product types or inferring payloads

failure: The first typecheck after adding the renderer-boundary regression rejected the intentionally throwing fixture as a void JSX component
root_cause: A function whose body only throws inferred void under the repository's React JSX typing
fix: Annotated the test-only BrokenOrganism fixture with ReactElement; no production code or runtime behavior changed
lesson: Intentionally failing React fixtures still need an explicit element return type so typecheck validates the boundary rather than the fixture inference

failure: The first focused Vitest command reported no test files
root_cause: The command was run from the frontend package while still passing a repository-root-prefixed test path
fix: Reran the same focused test with the package-relative path and reached the intended TDD failure
lesson: When a package script reports no tests, normalize the filter path relative to its configured working directory before diagnosing product behavior

failure: The post-change typecheck rejected Array.prototype.at in the new sampler regression
root_cause: The frontend TypeScript target does not include the ES2022 Array.at library even though the test runtime supports it
fix: Replaced callbacks.at(-1) with target-compatible callbacks[callbacks.length - 1] and kept the test behavior unchanged
lesson: Run typecheck after adding observability tests and use the repository's configured language target rather than the runtime's newer array helpers

failure: The full-suite revalidation command could not locate agent_coord.py before starting Vitest
root_cause: The lease command was chained from the frontend package directory, where the repository-level coordinator script is not present
fix: Let the already-started Vitest process finish, then claimed the writer lease from the repository root without chaining commands
lesson: Run coordination commands from the repository root and keep lease operations separate from package test processes so a path error cannot obscure test evidence

failure: The new ambient-motion control regression persisted the preference but the label did not update in the first test run
root_cause: The generated reduced-motion store intentionally returns a no-op subscription when matchMedia is unavailable, while the product shell relied only on that external-store update
fix: Added product-owned manual toggle state in LivingWorkspaceShell so the explicit control updates immediately while continuing to delegate the preference to the shared store
lesson: A product-owned accessibility control needs an immediate local response even when an optional platform subscription is unavailable; keep that fallback at the shell boundary instead of editing generated code

failure: The first handoff attempt was rejected because the short builder lease had expired during the long verification sequence
root_cause: The lease duration ended while the full suite and live browser revalidation were running, leaving no active writer lease at handoff time
fix: Reacquired the builder lease from the repository root and immediately completed the handoff without changing the worktree
lesson: For long evidence runs, re-check the coordination lease immediately before handoff and reacquire it only when no writer is active

failure: The first reviewer-inbox command used an unsupported --for option
root_cause: The coordination CLI requires the recipient via --agent and does not accept --for
fix: Reran the read-only inbox query with --agent codex
lesson: Check the coordination subcommand's declared flags when refreshing a handoff; keep an incorrect query separate from product evidence

failure: The first background-tab regression reported a false dropped-frame sample
root_cause: The fixture returned a constant mocked performance clock when the visibility event reset the previous timestamp, so the first visible callback measured the entire simulated pause
fix: Discard the first foreground frame after a visibility transition, then rerun the focused test successfully
lesson: Lifecycle-aware performance samplers should explicitly discard transition frames instead of assuming event-time and frame-time clocks are identical

failure: The first canon-gate command targeted scripts/check_css_canon.py and scripts/check_canon_frozen.py, which are not present in the isolated worktree
root_cause: The repository keeps these canon tools under tools/, while the frozen-core checker remains under scripts/
fix: Located the authoritative tool paths with rg --files and reran tools/check_css_canon.py, tools/check_canon_frozen.py, and scripts/check_frozen_core.py successfully
lesson: Resolve gate ownership from the current worktree before running evidence commands; do not infer tool locations from an older layout

failure: The first reduced-motion shell test looked for Emergency Stop with title case, but the existing accessible label is sentence case
root_cause: The test assertion did not match the product's already-established public label
fix: Corrected the assertion to use the measured accessible name 'Emergency stop' and reran the focused file successfully at 1 file / 8 tests
lesson: For accessibility regressions, assert against the existing accessible contract exposed by the DOM rather than inventing a capitalization variant

failure: Keeping the spine-flash point count fixed did not remove the live BufferGeometry warning
root_cause: The frame loop was calling BufferGeometry.setFromPoints() on Drei's LineGeometry, which uses interleaved instanceStart/instanceEnd segments rather than a regular position buffer
fix: Mutated the existing Drei segment attributes in place and isolated the updater in lineGeometry.js; a fresh preview then emitted no BufferGeometry warning
lesson: A fixed logical point count is insufficient when a renderer wrapper has a different geometry contract; trace the runtime object's attributes before choosing an update API

failure: The first post-evidence JSONL validation command treated the PowerShell-escaped regex as a literal and reported a false parse failure
root_cause: The shell wrapper over-escaped the JavaScript newline regex before passing it to node
fix: Rerun the same read-only validation with a PowerShell literal command so Node receives split(/\r?\n/)
lesson: When validating append-only JSONL from PowerShell, use a literal command or an explicit file-reading script and distinguish shell-quoting failures from data corruption

failure: The first port-check invocation ran from the repository root, where the frontend-only npm script does not exist
root_cause: The constrained gate bundle used the frontend workdir for the package scripts but the repository workdir for the frontend port-check script
fix: Reran npm run port:check from frontend/ so the authoritative fail-closed lab-source diagnostic could be observed
lesson: Keep package-owned frontend gates in the frontend workdir even when repository-level Python integrity gates run beside them

failure: The first Phase 4 evidence command accepted the symbolic tip HEAD and wrote an artifact that the ledger attach tool could not consume
root_cause: The evidence runner accepts a string argument but the attach contract requires a resolved 40-character commit SHA
fix: Deleted the invalid uncommitted artifact and reran the real probes with the exact resolved PR-head SHA 164c7d572fc6c777822fe70b054dbe61bc7c32a7
lesson: Resolve and validate the exact commit SHA before starting any evidence-producing operation; a passing probe is not attachable evidence until its identity satisfies the downstream contract

failure: The first repository-wide backend result was not attributable to product behavior
root_cause: A long .codex worktree triggered Windows path-length and credential-shaped path checks, and an explicitly external temporary data root violated the privacy test's project-containment assumption
fix: Recreated the runner at the explicitly short C:\w root and kept both pytest and AIOS test-data roots below that project root; retained the one remaining organ-ledger failure as baseline evidence
lesson: Runner path and temporary-data placement are part of the test fixture; isolate them before classifying a full-suite failure

failure: The first evidence commit was not a fast-forward candidate for PR #361
root_cause: PR #361 had advanced from 68f44fd2 to fc8ee90a through a master merge after the evidence worktree was created
fix: Stopped before force-push, created a fresh checkout at the observed PR head, and reran the exact-tip evidence operation
lesson: Remote PR history must be re-read immediately before publishing evidence; never force-push an attestation generated for an obsolete tip

failure: The first long-run browser soak accepted a replacement about:blank tab as if it were a loaded renderer
root_cause: The browser daemon reset between chain batches, while the collector only parsed the metric JSON and did not validate page identity
fix: Stopped the invalid run, added a reusable collector that requires one canvas, at least 50 DOM nodes and a live managed performance probe on every batch, and preserved the run as invalid evidence
lesson: Long-running browser evidence must validate page identity at each sample; a metric-shaped response from an empty replacement document is not product evidence

failure: The first repaired collector invocation still sent malformed command tuples and the later browser run lost its renderer process
root_cause: Windows PowerShell piped the outer tuple array through ConvertTo-Json as {value,Count} objects, and the headless browser manager remained unstable across relaunches
fix: Serialized with ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @($steps), relaxed error handling only around the browse.exe process boundary, and required structured loaded-scene identity before accepting a batch
lesson: Test the collector's host-shell serialization separately from product metrics, and treat browser-manager loss as invalid evidence rather than as a product failure

failure: The first post-change smoke probe failed before the browser ran because of nested PowerShell quoting, and a follow-up diagnostic used an incorrect browse.exe path
root_cause: Inline JavaScript with nested quote styles was embedded directly in a PowerShell string and the second command was typed against a nonexistent dist subpath
fix: Built the chain as PowerShell command tuples and used the verified browse.exe path before accepting the loaded-scene probe
lesson: For browser evidence, construct nested commands as serialized tuples and verify the executable path before interpreting any result as product evidence

failure: The new single-chain 30-minute soak did not produce a first batch because the browser server disconnected and timed out during startup
root_cause: The headless browser daemon remains unstable under a long requested chain even after removing per-batch invocation resets
fix: Recorded completedSamples=0, preserved the short two-batch validation, and left the 30-minute acceptance gate open
lesson: A collector can eliminate its own reset boundary but must not imply that the host browser is persistent; classify startup/connection loss as unavailable evidence, not as a product result

failure: The high-tier verification-fail gallery screenshot timed out and left a boot/loading image after the browser harness reset the tab
root_cause: The throttled WebGL browser could assert the selected DOM fixture but could not reliably settle the heavier scene before the screenshot timeout
fix: Excluded that image from the report, retained only the inspected resting capture, and recorded verification-fail/worker-burst as DOM/state assertions
lesson: Do not accept a screenshot merely because its selector exists; require scene readiness and inspect the pixels before linking a visual state artifact

failure: The high-tier verification-pass gallery transition lost the browser daemon before a settled capture
root_cause: The available headless WebGL environment is throttled and unstable when remounting the heavier high-tier state
fix: Accepted only the loaded low-tier reduced-motion failure capture and kept the high-tier pass evidence open
lesson: A quality-tier transition must be settled and pixel-inspected before it can support a visual acceptance claim; browser connection loss is unavailable evidence

failure: A standalone screenshot invocation restarted the QA browser onto a blank page after a valid interaction chain
root_cause: The browser daemon did not persist between separate screenshot invocations in this environment
fix: Excluded the blank PNG and reran navigation, fixture selection, settle, viewport reset and screenshot in one chain; inspected the replacement before linking it
lesson: For unstable browser daemons, the screenshot must be produced inside the same bounded chain that establishes the page and settled state

failure: The first authenticated backend setup created a disposable operator successfully, but the one-time enrollment credential was not retained in the same process as the later chat attempt; the shell SSE client also buffered its output
root_cause: The setup and journey were split across commands, and Invoke-WebRequest buffers an open event stream
fix: Stopped the disposable server, started with a fresh isolated data directory, and kept enrollment, login, streaming chat and mirror read in one bounded httpx process with no credential output
lesson: For one-time identity ceremonies and SSE evidence, use one process from credential issuance through terminal frame; never assume a buffered shell response proves stream completion

failure: The first attempt to continue the gallery matrix reused stale browser references after the daemon dropped
root_cause: Accessibility references belong to the previous browser page/session and are invalid after a daemon restart
fix: Excluded that chain and reran each tier from a fresh goto, canvas wait and snapshot before selecting fixtures
lesson: Browser matrix evidence must re-establish page identity and references for every chain; never interpret empty or stale-reference output as a state result

failure: The first approval probe completed without visible captured output and left its disposable instance enrolled, so a follow-up attempt received the expected 409 enrollment response
root_cause: The long streaming shell invocation was not retained as an interactive session, and the retry did not first reset the exact temporary instance
fix: Inspected the exact server processes and temporary directory, stopped both service processes, removed only that verified temporary directory, then reran with an unbuffered process and explicit session polling
lesson: For long live evidence, retain the process session and reset the exact disposable identity store before retrying a one-time enrollment ceremony

failure: The first cleanup pass could not remove one read-only rollback object in the disposable backend directory
root_cause: The backend's rollback object store contained a read-only file after the service stopped
fix: Confirmed the target directory was the exact disposable path, then retried removal with a narrow permission-reset handler and verified the directory was absent
lesson: Disposable backend cleanup must handle read-only rollback artifacts explicitly; verify the exact path before changing permissions or deleting it

failure: A disposable rollback cleanup left training_ground/.git pointing at a deleted temp repository, causing the next pre-create snapshot to fail closed
root_cause: The rollback engine intentionally leaves a gitdir pointer in the sandbox, but the test teardown removed the external rollback database without restoring the sandbox metadata
fix: Stopped the service, verified the pointer target was the exact deleted disposable path, rebuilt only the ignored training_ground rollback metadata from the current sandbox files, and confirmed its nested repository was clean
lesson: Every disposable rollback run must restore or remove its sandbox git pointer before deleting the external rollback database; otherwise the next supervised write correctly refuses before mutation

failure: The first passing development verification emitted a transient pass but the model repeated create_file and hit the loop-safety stop before durable verification was recorded
root_cause: The approval replay resumed the original create request and the model did not understand that forced verification was terminal
fix: Retried with an explicit instruction to call no tools after the approved replay and to end after the automatic verifier result; the stream reached done and the cortex bus recorded verification.completed passed=true
lesson: A transient verifier frame is insufficient evidence; require terminal done plus the durable verification event before claiming a verified live turn

failure: A browser interaction command lost the page between invocations and attempted to use an empty or stale DOM reference
root_cause: The headless browser daemon is ephemeral under repeated command failures and can restart at about:blank between calls
fix: Re-established the exact URL and page identity, waited for the interactive surface, then used fresh accessibility snapshots and direct DOM queries for every accepted observation
lesson: Never carry browser references across a daemon restart; a successful screenshot or snapshot must follow a fresh page identity and a clean interaction path

failure: The 150-batch headless chain timed out at startup and produced no accepted sample
root_cause: The browse daemon could serve a warmed page but lost its renderer while processing the large chain payload, so its blank replacement page failed the canvas/scene validity check
fix: Stopped accepting the chain as evidence, used a persistent Codex in-app browser tab, and added a localhost-only numeric DOM probe so the isolated inspection context could read the existing bounded metrics
lesson: A large browser command is not equivalent to a long-run page; require persistent page identity across the entire window and fail closed on any blank or replaced page

failure: The persistent worker-burst tab disappeared from the active browser session after 98 samples, before the requested 30-minute window completed
root_cause: The browser automation session stopped accepting the DOM handle during the 20th sampling window; URL/title polling remained cached but tab inventory confirmed the handle was no longer present
fix: Re-polled the same tab and browser inventory, accepted only the authoritative 1,116,942 ms prefix, refused to stitch a replacement run, stopped the server, and recorded the run as partial
lesson: A persistent page must remain addressable for the complete soak; cached URL/title values cannot extend evidence after the tab handle disappears

failure: One DOM sample timed out while the visible worker-burst soak was still running
root_cause: The browser inspection call exceeded its selector wait during a long-running page observation, while the page itself remained addressable
fix: Stopped at the last authoritative sample, re-polled the same handle and browser inventory, confirmed the exact URL, selected fixture and empty error log, then resumed sampling without filling the observation gap
lesson: Treat an observation timeout as an evidence boundary until same-handle identity and error state are re-established; recovery is acceptable only when the page remains the same live tab

failure: The attempted npm run port-unit command failed before running any tests
root_cause: The frontend package exposes the managed-source unit guard as test:port; port-unit is only a historical shorthand in continuity prose, not an npm script
fix: Read package.json, reran npm run test:port from frontend, and recorded the separate port:check blocker accurately
lesson: Resolve gate names from the current package manifest before running or reporting them; a missing script is an invocation error, not a product failure

failure: A read-only JSONL validation command failed with a Python SyntaxError before parsing the notebook
root_cause: PowerShell and embedded Python quoting truncated the f-string expression
fix: Treat the command as invalid evidence and rerun validation with a simpler command that avoids nested quoting
lesson: Keep cross-shell validation probes structurally simple; never treat a malformed probe as a repository or notebook failure

failure: A read-only ripgrep search included a POSIX wildcard path that Windows treated as an invalid filename
root_cause: The search command passed frontend/src/superbrain/lib/aiosAdapter* as a literal path instead of using ripgrep's pattern matching
fix: Discarded the partial search output and reran targeted searches with Windows-safe paths; no repository state or evidence was changed
lesson: On Windows, keep wildcard expansion inside ripgrep patterns or enumerate paths explicitly; a malformed search probe is not product evidence

failure: The first backend test invocation used a relative virtual-environment path unavailable inside the managed worktree, and the corrected full backend suite completed with 23 failures
root_cause: The worktree has no copied .venv, so PowerShell could not resolve .venv\Scripts\python; the shared interpreter then exposed existing backend/security/ledger failures unrelated to this frontend-only diff
fix: Reran with the existing main-checkout interpreter against the managed worktree, captured the complete failure summary, and kept the backend failures explicit rather than bypassing them
lesson: For isolated Windows worktrees, invoke the shared interpreter by absolute path and classify full-suite failures against the branch file list before claiming a green ship

failure: The first two continuity patches used stale expected text after selecting master's RESUME side
root_cause: The conflict-resolution working tree had current master wording and line breaks that differed from the earlier inspection excerpt
fix: Re-read the exact current lines and applied narrower patches; no product state or conflict resolution was changed by the failed probes
lesson: After selecting a merge side, inspect the actual working-tree text again before applying continuity patches; avoid relying on pre-restore excerpts

failure: The first JSONL validation probe failed with a Python SyntaxError before parsing either notebook
root_cause: PowerShell escaping truncated the embedded Python command around the encoding argument
fix: Discarded the malformed probe and reran the same read-only validation with shell-safe quoting; the corrected probe printed JSONL OK
lesson: Keep cross-shell notebook validation commands simple and treat a syntax failure before parsing as tooling noise, not evidence of invalid project state

failure: The final port:check command was initially launched from the repository root, where the npm script does not exist
root_cause: Combined final checks reused the repository-root working directory instead of frontend/ for an npm script owned by the frontend package
fix: Re-ran npm run port:check from frontend/; it passed with 193 files and changed=[]; the earlier git diff --check had already passed
lesson: Run package-owned npm gates from their owning package directory, even when adjacent repository-level guards run at the root

failure: Three plan documents were created with a relative apply_patch path that resolved in the main checkout even though shell commands targeted the isolated worktree.
root_cause: The patch tool uses the calling task's main checkout as its relative path root; exec_command workdir does not change that root.
fix: Moved only those three newly created documents into the isolated worktree after confirming they were untracked and destinations absent; checked that pre-existing main-checkout paths remained.
lesson: For linked-worktree edits from this task, use an explicit ../.codex/worktrees/gagos-living-being-v2/ai-editor path with apply_patch and verify target status.

failure: The default parallel frontend baseline reported 14 failed tests across 4 files, including timeouts and duplicate UI matches.
root_cause: The same unchanged 4782cfa3 tree passed all 953 tests with one fork worker and file parallelism disabled; the exact interaction between parallel scheduling and shared UI state remains unisolated.
fix: Repeated the full suite with the supported serial flags; 175 files / 953 tests passed.
lesson: Use the documented serial frontend gate on this checkout and distinguish concurrency-sensitive failures from deterministic product regressions.

failure: A baseline command used unsupported --minWorkers, and npm exec -- vitest run -- --help started tests instead of printing help.
root_cause: Vitest 5.0.1 has no --minWorkers option and npm exec argument separators did not invoke the intended CLI help path.
fix: Read supported flags from frontend/node_modules/.bin/vitest.cmd run --help; used --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism for the verified serial run.
lesson: Check the installed Vitest CLI directly before composing worker flags; preserve the command output and exit handle.

failure: The first writer claim used a new ticket-level task id that the local coordination database did not know.
root_cause: The prior RESUME named the broad goal task id, but the local coordination database had no task record after session/worktree continuity was restored.
fix: Inspected the only two dirty files and inbox, routed the existing goal id to Codex, then claimed that same id with --adopt-dirty.
lesson: Before claiming a resumed dirty worktree, reconcile RESUME's goal id with agent_coord state; if absent, route the existing goal id instead of inventing a per-ticket id, then explicitly adopt only after reviewing the dirt.

failure: Attempted to use an Edge browser provider and read browser/WebGL identity through the in-app read-only page inspector; the provider was unavailable and those identity APIs were not exposed.
root_cause: The current browser inventory contains only the Codex in-app browser, whose inspection surface exposes page data and screenshots but not the browser build, navigator or WebGL context identity.
fix: Captured only published content-free scene attributes, screenshot, accessibility state and console logs; documented browser/host/GPU identity as unknown and retained zero acceptance credit.
lesson: Before promising a named-device browser run, confirm the selected browser provider can expose its build and active adapter. Do not infer hardware identity from a localhost render or replace unavailable metadata with a guess.

failure: A fresh Windows worktree refused source restore because six managed files no longer matched their exact v1 hashes after Git normalized mixed line endings.
root_cause: The source manifest hashed raw bytes including mixed CRLF/LF, but the committed Git tree preserved normalized text and could not recreate those original newline bytes in another checkout.
fix: Verified every old lab file against its v1 accepted digest and every normalized file against the new checkout, then migrated to manifest v2 hashing after CRLF-to-LF normalization; real edits still fail closed.
lesson: Hash managed text using an explicitly documented newline canonical form when Git may convert EOLs; do not weaken content checking or regenerate a trust baseline without matching the existing accepted source.

failure: Exploratory test probes targeted local Close controls on embedded Files/Memory surfaces, and a proposed focus assertion expected a rail trigger to survive closing its own selected workspace.
root_cause: The panel components render in embedded mode without their own Close controls, and closing a selected workspace removes its rail trigger during the same React update; a focus restore issued before commit can target a transient node.
fix: Removed the invalid child-close probes, verified the shell Escape/Close path, and kept a stable Conversation fallback for triggers that dismissals remove.
lesson: Inspect the actual embedded rendering contract and trigger lifecycle before writing UI selectors or asserting post-dismissal focus; a mounted parent does not guarantee its selected child trigger survives.

failure: The first new focus regression queried a heading by text but the embedded History panel contains an h2 and h3 with the same accessible name.
root_cause: The assertion selected a duplicate accessible label without scoping to the selected workspace region or heading level, so the run failed before exercising the intended post-close focus behavior.
fix: Scope the assertion to the selected-workspace region and level-2 heading, then rerun until the test exposed focus remaining in the hidden surface.
lesson: For repeated UI labels, scope semantic queries to the owning region and role level so a test failure provides evidence about behavior rather than selector ambiguity.

failure: The guarded source restore in the fresh worktree failed to resolve the TypeScript package before creating the ignored authoring lab.
root_cause: The new worktree had no frontend/node_modules, while the sync tool imports TypeScript during manifest processing.
fix: Installed exact lockfile dependencies with npm ci, reran guarded restore, then verified all 193 managed files with port:check.
lesson: In a dependency-free worktree, restore the package-lock-pinned toolchain before invoking the source sync; do not bypass the guarded sync or hand-copy managed source.

failure: The first full-file patch payload for the source sync tool failed JavaScript parsing because the embedded source contained an unescaped template delimiter; a later context-sensitive patch also did not match the merge-conflicted file.
root_cause: The patch generator nested the target module's template strings inside its own template literal, and the supplied conflict context did not exactly match the current merge block.
fix: No patch was applied by the failed attempts. Rebuilt the source with a quote-safe literal, applied it through apply_patch, then passed node syntax checks and test:port 16/16.
lesson: For generated whole-file patch bodies, avoid nested template delimiters or use a quote-safe raw literal; inspect the exact merge stage before writing contextual patches.

failure: The first five-second full frontend pass had two load timeouts; a --isolate=false retry produced broad cross-file global-state failures; port:check could not run in the isolated worktree.
root_cause: The tests were running under four-worker resource load and exceeded Vitest's default timeout; disabling isolation allowed shared globals to leak across files. The ignored authoring lab was absent from this worktree.
fix: Both timed-out specs passed in isolation, and a normal fork-pool run with --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=10000 passed 177 files / 977 tests. Left the missing lab source untouched and reported port:check unavailable.
lesson: When test timeouts cascade, preserve per-file isolation and increase only the bounded worker/time allowance; do not use a non-isolated run as product evidence or regenerate source baselines to work around a missing worktree prerequisite.

failure: The in-app browser rejected a file URL for the SVG proposal.
root_cause: Browser URL policy blocks worktree-local file URLs and explicitly disallows alternate viewers or indirect browser workarounds.
fix: Stopped preview attempts and reported XML/aspect-ratio validation only; made no visual-preview claim.
lesson: Treat a browser URL denial as a hard boundary; use only a materially different in-scope check such as source/XML validation, or ask the user to open the artifact themselves.

failure: The first focused HUD-nerve implementation passed the screen center to a helper that expected the lower panel rim; the regression failed at y=-0.022 versus the expected lower rim at y=-0.5, and TypeScript caught an extra half-height argument.
root_cause: The geometry helper contract and its caller/test fixture disagreed about whether the input point was the panel center or its lower rim.
fix: Pass the already transformed lower-rim vector through both renderer and test; keep the expected rim point independently derived in the fixture.
lesson: Name and test 3D anchor inputs explicitly (center vs rim) at the call boundary; a normalized screen-up vector does not supply the panel's half-height by itself.

failure: The first live R3F gallery render crashed after a test-oriented data-focus-seat attribute was passed into a Line scene object, although component tests passed.
root_cause: A DOM-like test double accepted an arbitrary data attribute that React Three Fiber rejects when applying props to a Three.js object.
fix: Removed the unsupported scene prop, tested the actual path direction from captured coordinates, and rerendered the gallery in the browser.
lesson: After every nontrivial R3F prop/geometry change, run an actual local scene render; mocked DOM output is insufficient compatibility evidence.

failure: The first frontend test invocation passed --minWorkers=1 to the installed Vitest CLI, which rejected the unknown option before any tests started.

failure: The first replay-gap regression asserted a verified baseline before the initial stream had crossed sync_complete, so the presentation correctly reported stale instead of reaching the intended stale-receipt assertion.

failure: The second replay-gap regression attempt crossed the initial freshness barrier but still asserted a completed verified result while the seeded turn remained in the active phase.

failure: The product-source restore guard refused the fresh worktree because four managed product files had drifted from the source manifest; the command stopped during preflight and wrote no files.

lesson: Before editing a managed product source, verify source/lab/manifest alignment; when continuing a dirty branch, reconcile inherited product deltas before adding more changes.

failure: The combined source-recovery and temporary-cleanup PowerShell command was rejected by the execution safety wrapper before it ran; a later exact-path temp cleanup command was also blocked.

lesson: Do not bundle a valid reversible source migration with recursive cleanup. Keep recovery steps independently inspectable and avoid cleanup if the safety layer declines it.

failure: The full Python gate showed a failure at 9% and was stopped at 13%; the isolated failing test reproduced the red result.

failure: The first memory JSONL validation command reported malformed rows because its JavaScript newline regex was over-escaped.

failure: The first focused visibility-test runner response omitted its active process/session identifier, so its completion could not immediately be attributed to that call.

failure: A combined checkpoint patch was rejected because a CEO-log context line was accidentally placed in the RESUME.md hunk; the first follow-up repeated the mismatched file context.

failure: The managed Superbrain port initially failed first on mirrorStore.test.ts and then on mirrorStore.ts because the generated product contained a worker snapshot regression and implementation not yet present in the ignored authoring lab.

failure: The first frontend typecheck left a nullable snapshot cursor unresolved despite Number.isSafeInteger and a separate boolean alias proving its presence to a human reader.

failure: The first full Python run in the moved short-path test checkout failed because inspect.getsource could not find the decoy function's source.

failure: The first compact-workspace regression run failed because the new test referenced `within` without importing it, so that run could not prove the intended product gap.

failure: Initial short-root pytest probes used --basetemp=C:/g1 outside the conftest-owned session root, then a PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT-only run placed AIOS_DATA_DIR outside the repository and failed the privacy assertion.

failure: A checkpoint patch used a relative tools.apply_patch path while assuming exec_command's workdir controlled its root; it modified the main checkout's RESUME instead of the managed worktree and replaced the previous text.

failure: Both hosted format-gate runs failed after PR #406 was opened, despite targeted Ruff lint passing locally.

failure: The full Python suite showed three failures then spent several minutes at 93%; it was interrupted before pytest printed a summary.

failure: The corrected full Python run still failed two `/ready` tests because the C: volume fell to 288,141,312 free bytes during the suite, below the configured 536,870,912-byte minimum.

fix: No code or test threshold changed. The generated test run ended, but post-run free space remained 530,726,912 bytes. Request adequate operator-provided C: headroom (recommend at least ~300 MB beyond current free space) before rerunning.

failure: A full pytest --cov run continued beyond the 30-minute Codex builder lease; I did not renew the lease while it ran. It emitted F markers, then was interrupted near 76% after free C: space fell from 1.47 GB to about 110 MB; no final summary was captured.

fix: Stopped the test process once disk was far below the configured floor, confirmed no Python test processes remained, inspected recent candidate temp directories without deleting files, checked the coordination inbox, and reacquired the dirty builder lease before further edits. Do not rerun until at least 812 MB is free.
lesson: Before any long gate, verify the executable path from the worktree, renew/heartbeat the writer lease before expiry, and monitor C: with a hard stop above the readiness floor. An interrupted suite is red/incomplete; never report its partial markers as a complete diagnosis.
